sections.content: How many people stayed in Accrington after gaining qualifications?

Accrington is a medium-sized town in the North West. Accrington does not have its own university.

Accrington has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Accrington ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,955 state-school pupils from Accrington who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 545 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 655 (34%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Accrington to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Accrington's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Accrington in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Accrington move to?

Of Accrington's graduates, 185 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 60 of those graduates (32%) were living fairly locally, in the Blackburn travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Accrington's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 190 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 110 of those qualified non-graduates (58%) were living fairly locally, in the Blackburn travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Accrington's GCSE cohort:

  • 60 graduates left the North West
  • 45 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 23% of graduates and 31% of qualified non-graduates living in Accrington had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 455 graduates and 660 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Accrington. This is compared with the 545 graduates and 655 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of the graduates had also lived in Accrington as GCSE pupils, while 23% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Accrington in 2018 to 2019, 68% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 31% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
